gloss: how many days; several days; what day of the month

definitions.explanation: Asks or refers to an unspecified number of days. Slightly formal or literary; in casual speech, {何日|なんにち} is far more common.

examples.japanese: {幾日|いくにち}も{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{続|つづ}いた。
examples.english: It rained for many days on end.

examples.japanese: {幾日|いくにち}{過|す}ぎただろうか。
examples.english: How many days have passed, I wonder.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{返事|へんじ}を{待|ま}たずに{幾日|いくにち}も{連絡|れんらく}を{続|つづ}けた。
examples.english: He kept contacting them for days on end without waiting for a reply.

notes:
Compound of {幾|いく} (how many; some) + {日|にち} (day). Has a literary or slightly formal feel and most often appears in the pattern {幾日|いくにち}も (for many days). In casual everyday speech, use {何日|なんにち} for 'how many days?'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {幾日|いくにち}も: for many days; day after day
- {幾日|いくにち}{過|す}ぎる: many days pass
- {幾日|いくにち}も{前|まえ}: many days ago

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {何日|なんにち}: how many days; what day — everyday standard form
- {幾日間|いくにちかん}: for how many days
- {数日|すうじつ}: several days — neutral, common in writing
